A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Branch-and-Browse work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison. All pages were inspected; neither version contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original WebArena success rates, runtime ablations, and sensitivity experiments on search depth and branching.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional WebArena results for a SteP hybrid and VisualWebArena evaluation in Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 introduces a SteP-augmented variant that replaces the ReAct-style policy at node expansion with SteP sub-policies. Search, replay, background reasoning, pruning and memory retain their default logic. The expanded scoring description documents details without establishing a change to the original implementation.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from WebArena to VisualWebArena, covering Classifieds, Reddit and Shopping with multimodal observations and visual grounding requirements. This materially broadens the tested task and observation conditions while retaining the original WebArena coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Branch-and-Browse + SteP as an evaluated comparison variant alongside the original framework. All earlier WebArena baselines remain; standalone SteP was already included in v1.

E3.justification: The stated success-rate metric, successful-task timing rule, 812-task WebArena evaluation, default depth and branching factors of 5, and 10-step budget are retained. The added VisualWebArena evaluation explicitly uses the same model and budget conventions.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds a component-combination analysis testing whether SteP policies complement the existing search framework. The replay/background-reasoning ablations and depth/branching sensitivity experiments remain unchanged; the latter moves from Table 3 to Table 4.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing WebArena and ablation values are unchanged, but substantial new results are reported. Table 2 adds the SteP hybrid at 39.8% overall success alongside the original method's 35.8%. New Table 3 reports VisualWebArena overall success of 18.9% for the GPT-4o reactive baseline, 26.4% for Tree Search and 32.7% for Branch-and-Browse, plus site-specific results.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a bounded specification of the previously abstract utility score, v in [0,1], and describes retaining best-so-far values per subtask. This is a limited elaboration of the scoring definition. No proofs or theorems are added; renaming the transition operator from T to Trans is only notational.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about subtask-aware tree exploration, replay/background reasoning and page action memory. Their headline WebArena claims remain 35.8% success and a 40.4% execution-time reduction.

C2.justification: New discussion explains how subtask-conditioned scoring distinguishes progress from redundant retries, attributes the hybrid's benefits to SteP interaction routines, and interprets VisualWebArena results as evidence of multimodal applicability. The existing limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code repository link. Section 3.1 newly documents the LLM evaluator's conditioning inputs, score normalization and per-subtask bookkeeping, while Section 4.2 explains the SteP integration interface. These improve implementation documentation without establishing that the original implementation changed.

R1.justification: The new hybrid discussion explicitly connects the approach to prior policy-layer composition and develops its relationship to SteP beyond v1's suggested complementarity. The cited-work set is retained; updates to the VisualWebArena publication entry and LASER year are bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: Localized revisions expand the scoring explanation and organize Section 4.2 with WebArena, SteP-combination and VisualWebArena subheadings. v2 also adds acknowledgements and corrects terminology, grammar, author-block punctuation and bibliographic details. The main section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the VisualWebArena table and a hybrid row with an updated caption in Table 2. The sensitivity table is retained as Table 4 and relocated within the layout. Figures 1–4 retain their content; other layout differences mainly reflect text reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the evidence for policy complementarity through the SteP comparison and broadens validation to multimodal tasks. Scoring details and the code link also improve reproducibility information. These gains are useful but bounded: the new VisualWebArena setup is only briefly specified, and the unchanged limitations paragraph still presents hybrid policy integration as future work.
